50289-social-environment-and-moral-progr.title: Moral Progress
50289-social-environment-and-moral-progr.creator: Unknown
50289-social-environment-and-moral-progr.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. question of the relation of morality to our existing social environment, it will be advisable to inquire what we mean by moral progress, and what evidence there is that any such progress has occurred in recent times, or even within the period of well-established history.

arxiv-2011-06754.title: Re-framing Incremental Deep Language Models for Dialogue Processing with Multi-task Learning
arxiv-2011-06754.creator: Morteza Rohanian, Julian Hough
arxiv-2011-06754.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Morteza Rohanian, Julian Hough. We present a multi-task learning framework to enable the training of one universal incremental dialogue processing model with four tasks of disfluency detection, language modelling, part-of-speech tagging, and utterance segmentation in a simple deep recurrent setting. We show that these tasks provide positive inductive biases to each other with the optimal contribution of each one relying on the severity of the noise from the task.

arxiv-2209-08393.title: Unavoidable Higgs coupling deviations in the Z 2 Z_{2} -symmetric Georgi-Machacek model
arxiv-2209-08393.creator: Carlos Henrique de Lima, Heather E. Logan
arxiv-2209-08393.description: Abstract The Z 2 Z_{2} -symmetric version of the Georgi-Machacek model does not possess a decoupling limit in which all the new particles can be made arbitrarily heavy, opening the possibility that the model can be entirely excluded if experiments reveal no deviations from the Standard Model.

arxiv-2302-05886.title: An unsupervised learning approach for predicting wind farm power and downstream wakes using weather patterns
arxiv-2302-05886.creator: Mariana C. A. Clare, Simon C. Warder, Robert Neal, B. Bhaskaran, Matthew D. Piggott
arxiv-2302-05886.description: Abstract Wind energy resource assessment typically requires the use of numerical models, but such models are too computationally intensive to consider multi-year or multi-decade timescales. Increasingly, unsupervised machine learning techniques are used to identify a small number of representative weather patterns that can help simulate long-term behaviour.

arxiv-2406-03223.title: Object Manipulation in Marine Environments using Reinforcement Learning Sponsor and financial support anonymous.
arxiv-2406-03223.creator: Ahmed Nader, Muhayy Ud Din, Mughni Irfan, Irfan Hussain
arxiv-2406-03223.description: Abstract Performing intervention tasks in the maritime domain is crucial for safety and operational efficiency. The unpredictable and dynamic marine environment makes the intervention tasks such as object manipulation extremely challenging. This study proposes a robust solution for object manipulation from a dock in the presence of disturbances caused by sea waves.

arxiv-2407-02881.title: ShiftAddAug: Augment Multiplication-Free Tiny Neural Network with Hybrid Computation
arxiv-2407-02881.creator: Yipin Guo, Zihao Li, Yilin Lang, Qinyuan Ren
arxiv-2407-02881.description: Abstract Operators devoid of multiplication, such as Shift and Add, have gained prominence for their compatibility with hardware. However, neural networks (NNs) employing these operators typically exhibit lower accuracy compared to conventional NNs with identical structures. ShiftAddAug uses costly multiplication to augment efficient but less powerful multiplication-free operators, improving performance without any inference overhead.

arxiv-2501-08956.title: Insights into Supermassive Black Hole Mergers from the Gravitational Wave Background
arxiv-2501-08956.creator: C. M. F. Mingarelli 1, L. Blecha 2, T. Bogdanović 3, M. Charisi 4,5, S. Chen 6, A. Escala 7, B. Goncharov 8,9, M. J. Graham 10, S. Komossa 11, S. T. McWilliams 12,13, D. A. Schwartz 14, J. Zrake 15
arxiv-2501-08956.description: Abstract At the Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics, participants of the rapid response workshop on the gravitational wave background explored discrepancies between experimental results and theoretical models for a background originating from supermassive black hole binary mergers. Underestimated theoretical and/or experimental uncertainties are likely to be the explanation.

arxiv-2501-09519.title: Multi-task deep-learning for sleep event detection and stage classification
arxiv-2501-09519.creator: Adriana Anido-Alonso, Diego Alvarez-Estevez
arxiv-2501-09519.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Adriana Anido-Alonso, Diego Alvarez-Estevez. Polysomnographic sleep analysis is the standard clinical method to accurately diagnose and treat sleep disorders. It is an intricate process which involves the manual identification, classification, and location of multiple sleep event patterns. This is complex, for which identification of different types of events involves focusing on different subsets of signals, resulting on an iterative time-consuming process entailing several visual analysis passes.

arxiv-2501-13211.title: Incorporating Magnetic Field Characteristics into EUV-Based Automated Segmentation of Coronal Holes
arxiv-2501-13211.creator: Jeremy A. Grajeda, Laura E. Boucheron, Michael S. Kirk, Andrew Leisner, C. Nick Arge, Jaime A. Landeros
arxiv-2501-13211.description: Abstract Coronal holes (CH) are magnetically open regions that allow hot coronal plasma to escape from the Sun and form the high-speed solar wind. This wind can interact with Earth’s magnetic field. For this reason, developing an accurate understanding of CH regions is vital for understanding space weather and its effects on Earth.

arxiv-2502-15287.title: Time Warp: The Gap Between Developers’ Ideal vs Actual Workweeks in an AI-Driven Era Thanks: 6 Contacts: chetanb@microsoft.com, brian.houck@microsoft.com, bash@microsoft.com. Thanks: 2 Sukrit Kumar and Drishti Goel are joint first authors of this work.
arxiv-2502-15287.creator: Sukrit Kumar 1 2 , Drishti Goel 4 2 , Thomas Zimmermann 7 , Brian Houck 4 6 , B. Ashok 5 6 , Chetan Bansal 4 6
arxiv-2502-15287.description: Abstract Software developers balance a variety of different tasks in a workweek, yet the allocation of time often differs from what they consider ideal. Identifying and addressing these deviations is crucial for organizations aiming to enhance the productivity and well-being of the developers.

arxiv-2503-15794.title: Finite-Horizon Discrete-Time Optimal Control for Nonlinear Systems under State and Control Constraints
arxiv-2503-15794.creator: Chuanzhi Lv, Hongdan Li, Huanshui Zhang
arxiv-2503-15794.description: Abstract This paper addresses the optimal control problem of finite-horizon discrete-time nonlinear systems under state and control constraints. A novel numerical algorithm based on optimal control theory is proposed to achieve superior computational efficiency, with the novelty lying in establishing a unified framework that integrates all aspects of algorithm design through the solution of forward and backward difference equations (FBDEs).

pmc-12812962.title: Multisensory nature-based Recharge Rooms’ effect on healthcare workers in a multicenter study
pmc-12812962.creator: Lily Cooke, Arianna Fiorentino, Abbey Sawyer, Neha S. Dangayach, Scott Sharples, Rena Szabo, B. Wade Hamilton, Mar Cortes, David Putrino
pmc-12812962.description: BackgroundHealthcare workers frequently experience significant levels of stress impacting wellbeing and performance. A previous single site study showed multisensory, naturalistic “Recharge Rooms” were associated with a self-reported improvement in stress across healthcare workers. Subsequently, rooms were constructed at multiple hospitals across the country to assess their effects in a multi-site study.

pmc-13238789.title: Does having bad epilepsy make you a good surgical candidate? A number needed to treat analysis
pmc-13238789.creator: Sallie Baxendale, Dominic Heaney, Matthew C Walker
pmc-13238789.description: Epilepsy surgery is an established treatment for drug‐resistant epilepsy, offering a realistic prospect of seizure freedom in well‐selected candidates. However, surgery is sometimes offered to individuals with a low probability of seizure freedom when it is framed as potentially “life‐saving” on the basis of the elevated mortality associated with uncontrolled epilepsy.
